subject: MMPBSA error with receptor prmtop but not clear how to fix Amber20

messages.author: Vaibhav Dixit
messages.body:
Dear All,
I'm getting the following error message while trying to run MMPBSA.py in
Amber20.
It says that the receptor mask overwritten with default, which I don't know
why it is doing even after I gave a specific receptor mask (1st residue is
my ligand in the trajectory). It also gives the bad atom type error, that
I got with Amber18 last month.
>From the output files (attached), it is not clear what is the exact nature
of the error, thus I have no clue how to proceed to fix the same.
Can you please help me understand why the dry prmtop is not compatible?
And how can I possibly attempt to get this analysis done?
My mmpbsa input file is given below.
Thanking you all in advance.
Best regards
mmpbsa input file:
(base) [exx.c107739 mmpbsa-6701-tyr]$ more mmpbsa-decomp.in
&general
startframe=1, endframe=100, interval=5,
verbose=2, keep_files=2, netcdf=1, receptor_mask=2-386,
strip_mask=:387-16750,
/
&gb
igb=5, saltcon=0.150,
/
&pb
istrng=0.15, fillratio=4.0,
/
&decomp
idecomp=1, print_res="56-57; 74-75; 167; 222; 225-227; 229-231; 272-273;
275-277; 336; 368; 370; 372-373"
dec_verbose=1,
/
Error message on the terminal
(base) [exx.c107739 mmpbsa-6701-tyr]$ MMPBSA.py -O -i mmpbsa-decomp.in -o
mmpbs-rouf-6701-tyr.dat -do decomp-rouf-6701-tyr.dat -sp
../rouf-6701-tyr-solv.prmtop -cp ../rouf-6701-tyr-dry.prmtop -lp
../tyr-dry.prmtop -y ../rouf-6701-tyr-solv-prod300.nc -rp
../rouf-6701-nolig-dry.prmtop
Loading and checking parameter files for compatibility...

I'm afraid, I still can't find this file inside the AmberTools folder,

OK.
Have you compiled AMBER20 using the legacy configure method or the new
cmake method?

should find that file in amber20_src/AmberTools/src/sander/mdread2.F90.
if you have compiled using the legacy method, then you files should in the
path where I sent previously.
Best Regards
Elvis

Best Regards
Elvis

messages.body:
Dear All and Elvis,
The GB calculation did work after recompling with the suggested changes.
But the PB calculation is failing with the following error messages.
Inspection of the output file shows that it did not find radii for the S
atom which has type "Y1" as defined by the MCPB.py tool which I had used
for building parameters for the co-factor.
Thus I'm wondering does this require adding similar lines in the PB section
of the mdread2.F90 file?
Please help me understand how should I try to fix this error?
Thank you and best regards.

messages.body:
Dear Elvis and All,
The PB calculation seems to be running fine now with the radiopt=0 option.
I'm trying with the serial version/mode. Once the serial jobs finish
correctly, then I will recompile, test the Amber parallel version and
resubmit these calculations to check for speed up gained.
Is it possible to estimate how much extra time the PB calculations are
likely to take than the GB? i.e. what is the expected scaling factor
between GB and PB calculations? For 20 frames the GB calculation took
about 30 minutes.
As I understand from the manual, MMPBSA runs only on CPU, please let me
know if GPU usage is possible.
Thank you very much for your valuable suggestions and support.
Best regards.

messages.body:
Dear Elvis and All,
The PB calculation initially terminated with an error for which there was a
fix in the amber archive.
It was about adding the ligand in the print_res option.
After that, the calculation has finished in 1 hr without error as shown
below.
Next, I want to analyze the GB-SA and PB-SA results for different ligands
and understand/correlate their binding Es and residue-wise comparison with
experimental data (ITC, spectroscopic and reaction rates).
I realize that there might be some caveats in such analysis and
interpretation and thus it will help if you can point towards any recent
reviews that might cover this topic and give some general guidance on
MMPBSA calculations.
The ref printed out by the script is from 2012, thus hoping that there
might be relevant updates which are a bit tricky to dig out from the vast
literature.
I just noticed the FEW options, is it expected to give similar/identical
results?
I have some questions about the FEW option, which I will post separately.
Thank you very much for your valuable suggestions and help.
best regards.
